questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Sample 2701: A spectrophotometer reports transmittance 0.653. What is the absorbance?

options.misconception: takes the log of absorbed rather than transmitted light
drops the minus sign in the absorbance definition
treats absorbance as the fraction of light absorbed

questions.explanation: Absorbance is the negative base-ten logarithm of transmittance, not simply one minus transmittance. Because transmittance is less than one, the logarithm is negative and the minus sign makes absorbance positive and additive.

provenance.author: bank-team-analychem
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Measurement 2702: A solution has absorbance 0.475. What fraction of incident light is transmitted?

options.misconception: treats absorbance directly as an absorbed fraction
uses a positive exponent instead of a negative one
applies the conversion in the wrong direction

questions.explanation: Transmittance is ten raised to the negative absorbance. It must lie between zero and one, so a positive exponent or treating absorbance as a fraction cannot be correct. The logarithmic relation makes equal absorbance steps equal multiplicative changes in transmittance.

questions.explanation: Absorbance is the negative base-ten logarithm of transmittance, not simply one minus transmittance. Because transmittance is less than one, the logarithm is negative and the minus sign makes absorbance positive and additive.

questions.stem: Aliquot 2800: A solution has absorbance 0.618. What fraction of incident light is transmitted?

options.misconception: uses a positive exponent instead of a negative one
applies the conversion in the wrong direction
treats absorbance directly as an absorbed fraction

questions.explanation: Transmittance is ten raised to the negative absorbance. It must lie between zero and one, so a positive exponent or treating absorbance as a fraction cannot be correct. The logarithmic relation makes equal absorbance steps equal multiplicative changes in transmittance.
